column1: # Per work-item duration estimates, in minutes, used ONLY to bin-pack the test
# matrix. Nothing about correctness depends on these numbers: a wrong estimate
# makes a leg longer or shorter than its neighbours, it never changes which
# tests run. Treat the file as a scheduling hint, not a specification.
# A shard of "-" means the package runs unsharded, and an unsharded package
# runs every tier in ONE invocation, so its tier here is "all". Only a sharded
# package is split into deterministic | coyote | chaos rows, because only there
# does the split buy concurrency rather than extra process starts.
# These are test times only. plan-test-matrix.py adds a fixed per-invocation
# overhead on top, so do not try to bake process start into the numbers here.
# Only non-trivial items are listed. Anything absent falls back to the defaults
# in plan-test-matrix.py, which are deliberately small: the long tail of this
# repository really is near-instant (37 of 46 packages run in about 0.1 min
# each), so defaulting them low is right and the packages that matter are all
# PROVENANCE. Every row below is MEASURED, from the first full-fan-out run of
# the matrix prototype (run 34378766327, 46 packages selected, all legs green).
# The figures are the wall-clock a work item took on its leg, which is test time
# plus that invocation's own process start, and they are what the aggregate
# report emits at the end of each run in exactly this format.
# The `bplustree` deterministic row is the critical path and the reason
# `bplustree-publicapi` was later split out of it: the trx for that leg showed
# 245s of test time, of which 66s was the 339 reflection-driven assertions in
# PublicApiContract alone. Its row here is a projection of the remainder and is
# the one number in this file that has not been directly observed.
